name: Ponte Vecchio
hint: The river runs high, so the arches must be shallow: spring them from low piers and keep everything below the road - the shops sit on top.

history.name: Ponte Vecchio
history.engineer: Traditionally Taddeo Gaddi (perhaps Neri di Fioravanti)
facts: Its arches are segmental: they rise only about a fifth of their span, so the bridge needed just two piers in the river.
Butchers, tanners and fishmongers once kept shops on the bridge; in 1593 Grand Duke Ferdinando I allowed only goldsmiths and jewellers.
In 1944 it was the only bridge in Florence that the retreating German army did not destroy.
history.why: Flat segmental arches let medieval Florence cross the Arno with few, slim piers - and still carry a whole street of shops, with the Vasari Corridor (1565) running above them.
